2010 Honda Ridgeline 4WD Crew Cab RTL - $14,995  Year: 2010 Make:Honda Model:Ridgeline Trim:4WD Crew Cab RTL Mileage:82,748 Stock #:4617 VIN:5FPYK1F56AB504200 Trans:Automatic Color:Black Vehicle Type:Truck State:NY Drive Train:4WD Engine:3.5L SOHC MPFI 24-valve VTEC V6 engine  Notes About this vehicle:Two OwnersNo accidents or damagesFirst owned in Nepean, ONRear privacy glassDual-zone automatic climate controlEight-way power driver seatUpgraded seven-speaker audio system with a six-CD changer and steering-wheel-mounted audio controls18-inch alloy wheelsFoglightsPower-sliding rear window, air-conditioning60/40-split rear seat with under-seat storageReview from Edmunds.com:The balance between form and function is something automotive designers are constantly wrestling with. In the case of the 2010 Honda Ridgeline, function is the clear winner. The midsize Ridgeline pickup may lack the macho attitude of many rivals, but it compensates with a healthy dose of pure unadulterated practicality. The result is a well-rounded midsize pickup with a unique combination of strengths.  Built on the same unibody platform as the Odyssey minivan and previous-generation Pilot SUV, the Ridgeline trades the enclosed rear cargo areas of those models for a 5-foot-long truck bed. Using these lighter-duty underpinnings gives the Ridgeline a number of advantages over traditional body-on-frame pickups, starting with noticeably better handling and a more carlike ride. A lower overall height also makes it easier to get in and out of the comfortable five-passenger cabin.  The Ridgeline's main attraction, however, is that 5-foot bed. Made out of a steel-reinforced composite material, the bed makes rust and dents a non-issue. While it's short by full-size pickup standards, there's still enough room for a pair of dirt bikes or an ATV with the tailgate lowered. It also incorporates two innovative features -- a large under-floor "trunk" compartment and a tailgate that both flips down and swings out like a door -- that are so useful, they make you wonder why nobody thought of them sooner.  While the Ridgeline is all the truck many pickup buyers will ever need, it's not for everybody. The standard all-wheel-drive system (there's no low-range gearing) and light-duty suspension make it unsuitable for serious off-roading. The mandatory V6 is adequate in normal driving, but it's noticeably less punchy than the V6s and V8s available elsewhere. Two other downsides are a modest 5,000-pound towing capacity and braking distances that are longer than normal for this class of vehicle.  Buyers who like to weigh all their options might also want to consider the midsize Ford Explorer Sport Trac and full-size Chevrolet Avalanche. Both represent similar efforts to re-imagine the traditional pickup truck for personal use, though neither attempt is quite as successful as the Ridgeline. Also, bigger trucks like the Dodge Ram and Toyota Tundra have more workhorse potential, and V6-powered versions of the midsize Nissan Frontier and Toyota Tacoma are sprightlier. Still, the 2010 Honda Ridgeline has got the functionality thing nailed for many shoppers in this segment. 1976 Cadillac Eldorado Convertible  This car was sold new in 1976 to a couple in New Britain CT. As they grew too old to drive the car, their son purchased the car in 1994. When his Dad passed away, the son had the car "gone through" and some body work done and the car repainted. He moved south to Old Saybrook CT and several years ago, as part of barter deal, the current owner came into possession of the car. As part of a large collection, the car was well maintained but not driven often and now as the collector is getting up in age a bit, it has been suggested that he start clearing out some of the cars.  This will be one of the first to go.  There are 82,000 miles on the 425 V8, which puts out 180 HP and 320 lb.ft.  She runs and floats well like any land yacht should. The current owner has replaced the radiator, hoses, belts, alternator, fuel lines, convertible top and frame, front tires, exhaust and brake master cylinder all in the last couple of years. However, despite the new exhaust there is till some unwanted rumble that is most probably a doughnut gasket at the funky crossover that these FWD Caddies have.  The black leather interior is in rather good shape, aside from a small tear in the driver headrest and some other small wear points. Very comfortable as any large boat or leather sofa would be.  The frame and most of the floors are solid and rot free.. However, the usual place for these to go bad.. has... The catalytic converter sits right in the center of the front floor and over heats and rusts out that floor section. This one has been haphazardly patched. The good news is as this is so typical, there are MULTIPLE sources for replacement pans for that section of floor.  It also seems that when the car was "gone through", whoever went through it, patched the emanating rust with Bondo. They can be clearly seen now in both front fenders, just behind the wheels, one side completely rotted away. Behind each rear wheel there is the beginning of rust bubbles so their fate would be similar to the fronts if evasive action isn't taken quickly.  As these were to be the "Last American Convertible", 14000 were ordered and produced and are still seen as relatively popular collector cars which have held their value. Concours quality cars going for near to $75,000.  This Eldo came equipped with the black leather interior; power windows; power locks; power steering; power top; power seats; power brakes (4 wheel discs, a highly prized option); auto climate control/AC (non operational, may need a charge, compressor spins); Soft ray tinted glass; remote mirrors; Tilt/telescoping steering wheel; intermittent wipers; auto dim headlights and the twilight sentinel.  She'll make a great summer cruiser as is, but she is worth investing the time and money into to make her great again.  Great, two owner car.  Asking price is $6200  Any questions, for many more photos and video, to schedule a time to see her or to make an offer, please don't hesitate to contact me.  Thanks for the interest.

Up for sale is my 1999 Porsche 911 Carrera 2 6 speed manual in excellent original condition, impeccable maintenance, and a number of rare options.  The car has 64,585 miles which will go up slightly as I will continue to drive this beauty.  I purchased this Carrera in December 2018 to augment my 1973 Porsche 911 longhood and it has been an incredible driver and fun sports car.  I am well versed in these cars as I have continuously owned at least one Porsche since 1981 including a rare Mexico Blue 1974 911 (which is featured in Leffingwell’s book), a show quality 1960 356 Roadster, a rare 1993 RS America, and others.  I am a 59 year old aeronautical engineer and current CEO of a consumer products company who impeccably chooses and maintains the cars that come through my “collection”.  I searched for almost 2 years for a great 99 Carrera 2 Coupe 6 speed manual… sure they made a few of these cars but so many a clapped out, have not had proper maintenance or were simply abused.  The ’99 is special as it is the only year to have a limited slip as an option, and even then less than 10% were fitted with it (this car has it!).  In addition, the 99s had a cable throttle (as opposed to the less sporting electronic throttle) and the much more robust dual row IMS bearing.  The 3.4 liter water cooled engine makes 296 horsepower and 258 ft*lbs or torque with reported 0-60 time below 5.0 seconds and 174mph top speed (not that I have ever tested it :o)  As most who are reading this will know, the Carrera 2 Coupe is virtually universally preferred over the Carrera $ (awd) and/or Cabriolet as it is lighter, more sporting and allows more road feel.  These cars truly are the best value in sports cars available today.  My car was fully optioned with the best sporting features including the aforementioned limited slip but it also has the not often seen factory sport design wheels, a rear window wiper (which one hardly ever sees) and of course classic black leather heated seats and aluminum accouterments.  The car was custom ordered as seen by the 09991 code (see below) by its original owner.   When I purchased the car I had it assessed by leading Porsche shop TRE Motorsports (this report is obviously available to interested buyers) and they did a deep inspection including a DME report (zero over revs in all ranges).  Dave (TRE owner) stated it was one of the best 996s he has seen and heartily recommended I purchase the car.  As many know the IMS has been Achilles heel of the 999 series of 911s (1999-2004) so even though my car had the dual row bearing, I spent over $5000 after purchasing the car to replace the IMS, RMS, clutch, and flywheel (in addition to other stuff like battery, battery loom, brakes, etc) to be sure this car was in optimal shape and ready for regular duty.  An LN Engineering bearing was used and the work was done by leading the leading Santa Barbara Porsche shop (Schneider Autohaus; receipt for work available to interested parties).  So why I am selling – two primary reasons:  both my son and I are having some significant health issues and upcoming medical bills make this car a luxury that I no longer feel is appropriate. Please take the time to read the posting. I list a lot of information with the purpose of answering most questions beforehand. This is a F350 single rear wheel Powerstroke 4x4.  it has about 220,000 miles manual six speed extended cab 33x12.50 tires, they are in really good shape  The bad: 1. both rear cab corners are rusted through. if i keep the truck long enough i will eventually fix these but i would rather sell as is.  2. Seat tear (3 inches) in the driver’s side. can be stitched up. one of the few things i never got to.  3. came from northern OH. So, it has some rust underneath. Not horrible, but more than my other 7.3 dually. 4. stereo is flaky on channel selection 5. The paint is OK. It has scratches and such 6. This may be good or bad depends on opinion; the muffler was removed by previous owner. Is a straight pipe back to the rear wheel. Not horribly loud, people that are use to quite cars will notice. I was never bothered by it and left it as it was.   The good: 1. The flat bed is basically brand new. No damage, just a little dingy, but it is in great shape. This is a $2000+ bed.  2. 7.3 diesel engine with moderate miles.  3. interior is clean, all vinyl has been repaired properly.  4. A basic TS-6 tuner came on the truck when i got it. works well. for me i keep it in lower setting. for me its a truck not a hot rod so never saw the need for the higher settings.  5. Really important: neither exhaust manifold is cracked. this tells me the tuner was never ran hard for long periods. if that is done to these trucks the rear of the manifold will crack.   The work that was done by me: I bought this truck as a back up to my 2002 7.3 dually. Drove it as it was for a while and then noticed the oil pan was leaking. It was rusting through. This is very common for these trucks up north. Problem is, it’s an engine pull to replace it. So I pulled the engine. Since this was being done, I figured I would go through and fix things I knew were issues on these 7.3s. I did these things on my dually as well years back, just part of the game on a 7.3. list of everything that I did: 1.	New oil pan and one piece gasket 2.	Replaced oil cooler O-rings and gaskets 3.	Replaced the turbo pedestal with a 1999 one without the exhaust heat up flap. 4.	Removed the “heat up” flap – useless feature 5.	Replaced the up-pipes with bellowed up pipes – THIS IS A BIG DEAL. Prevent future turbo leaks and power losses.  6.	Replaced oil filter mount housing. There was a crack in the old one.  7.	Replaced the passenger injector wiring harness plug.  8.	Replaced the throw-out bearing on the clutch since I was there 9.	Replaced pilot bearing 10.	Did not replace the clutch. It was in excellent shape.  11.	Obviously, fluids were changed.  12.	Relevant Turbo O-rings were replaced 13.	Most of the hard brake lines were replaced up front Back pressure test was done for turbo leaks and zero leaks were found. Boost will now climb to 25 psi or higher if you want it too.  So why am I selling it with all this work done? I bought this as a backup to my dually. After I owned it a little over a year I got the idea that I wanted a sports car as a secondary vehicle to my truck. On top of this, I have a few other cars. Simply put, I now have too many cars and don’t need this one. It would be great to keep. If for nothing else I like the 6 speed better than the auto in my dually, and the tires are far better in the mud. (This truck weighs about 7400 lbs, but is usable in the mud. ) However, paying taxes, maintenance, and insurance just doesn’t make sense to keep.   So long term, I want to sell the truck. It’s a 7.3 in really good mechanical shape and decent shape cosmetically. I have driven this truck on three- and four-hour drives and it did fine. I don’t need to sell in a hurry and as such will not give it away or just dump it. If still interested we will see if we can work out a price. But until you have seen the vehicle and can see its upside and down sides, you really cant discuss price.
